settings.title: Source
settings.text: Wild Cambodian agarwood from Assam, Florentine iris root aged for three years, and Madagascan pink pepper — harvested by hand.

settings.title: Compound
settings.text: Each extrait is compounded at an uncompromised 35% oil concentration, where traditional houses dilute to 12–15%.

settings.title: Macerate
settings.text: The unpolished mixture matures inside temperature-stabilised obsidian vaults for 90 days, so the molecules bind without harsh alcohol top notes.

settings.title: Finish
settings.text: Each flacon is laser-engraved with its batch code and compounding date, then hand-wrapped in matte black hardboard.

settings.label: Intensity
settings.text: Unusually high concentration requiring only 1–2 atomised sprays.

settings.question: How many sprays should I use?
settings.answer: One to two sprays is enough. At 35% concentration an extrait is considerably denser than an eau de parfum — apply to pulse points or clothing rather than layering.

settings.question: Which size should I choose?
settings.answer: If you haven't worn AGHA before, the Discovery Collection holds five of our extraits in 5 × 5 ml so you can wear each one for a few days before committing to a full flacon.

settings.question: What arrives in the box?
settings.answer: The numbered flacon, hand-wrapped in matte black hardboard, with a complimentary 5 ml sample.

settings.question: Why is every batch rested for 90 days?
settings.answer: Maceration lets the raw materials bind. Resting each batch in temperature-stabilised vaults removes the sharp alcohol edge you notice in the first minutes of many perfumes.
